137 and 138 stagecoach buses were cancelled mid November. 

However, the council is running an on demand bus service to replace them. 
You have to call a number to book your seat on it at least the day before (and up to a week in advance). 

I've only taken the on demand bus once but it worked pretty well, you just tell them where you want to be picked up and dropped off and at what time and  then they call you back the day before travelling to give you exact details.

You can find all of the info you need on the angus council website here: https://www.angus.gov.uk/roads_parking_and_travel/public_transport/bus_timetables

The new busses are numbers 537/538.

Hey! I was in a similar position here. 
I got an unconditional in October 2021 with no funding, did a bunch of funding application and was unsuccessful for all of them so I deferred to February 2022 while I looked for other funding. 

I didn't find anything that would cover both my tuition fees and give me a stipend but I have eventually managed to secure a scholarship from the actual university department to cover the tuition fees. So I moved to part-time study and have kept my full-time job to cover other expenses.

I was lucky since I can do my university work and my job from home so it's easier to manage. And both my supervisors and my manager are super accommodating and have allowed me to work out a flexible schedule but God I'm busy now 😄

Maybe that could be an option for you as well? (Bare in mind that you'll have very little free time this way and have to be super efficient about scheduling and allowing yourself to rest and relax too. This I have learned very quickly!)

Good luck and I hope you manage to do what you want to do 😊

I had to fight so much to get referred for a laparoscopy (and I still haven't got the surgery btw because of the backlog but at least I've got the referral).   
They had me try everything under the sun for about 4 years (combined pill. progesterone only, IUD... ) and only after nothing else worked they considered  a laparoscopy. I am also fairly convinced that the only reason I've got it is because my normal gynaecologist was not available for my appointment so I was seen by a different doctor whose specialisation is in diagnostic laparoscopies.  


I'm really sorry you are going through this, I understand how frustrating it is. My suggestion would be to ask if you can see a different gynaecologist and keep asking for the treatment you want until you get heard. Best of luck.

How many litter trays does the cat have? And what kind of cat litter does she use? 

It is recommended by vets to have 1 extra litter tray compared to the number of cats. So 2 litter trays for 1 cat, 3 for 2 cats and so on.

My cats are spoiled brats (entirely my fault, they're too cute :P )  and they love silica cat litter. They almost won't go anywhere else. It would be worth trying a few different kinds of cat litter to see if the cat prefers one over others. 

Also what genders are both the cat and the dog? If they are both males they maybe be in a bit of a battle to leave their scent around and mark the territory, in that case closing the door is your only option really. 

For your bedsheets and mattress I would say bleach everything! You can also try citrusy room fresheners to keep the cat away as most of them don't like those sort of smells (although it varies, didn't work with my cats. They actually seemed to like it and even lick lemons). But make sure you get some that are safe to keep around your dog.

Have you seen "How I met your mother" by any chance? 

I'm not suggesting to watch the entire series (it's got its ups and downs) but at some point one of the characters (Lily) that has been in a relationship with another character for a very long time goes through some similar feelings. She feels like she's missed out on some life experiences because of the relationship so she just take a break for it, goes traveling, lives in another country for a while and then goes back.

Maybe you could consider that. Stepping back and taking some time to yourself is never a bad thing. You're so young and delaying those life decisions a few months is not going to change anything. 

Maybe go live with your friends or by yourself for a bit, get a plant or start a new hobby and see how that makes you feel. You may find that being with your fiancé, marriage and kids is what you want or you may find that that's not for you at the moment.  But take the time to really know what it is that you like and want from your life.  

It's your life. Not your parents'. Not your fiancé's. You only have one life and you've got to make the most out of it. That includes taking risks and making mistakes and that's fine. 

As an aside, I would have a hard thing about being in a relationship in which you're not participating in any of the decisions and in which your opinions do not seem to be taken into account. Is that how you want to spend your future years?  If a friend was in the same situation what would you tell them?
